title: Day-zero accesses and priority skill map
content:
Purpose: capture a pragmatic, low-friction Day 0 access policy + an early 30-day priority-skill map to support quiet-start onboarding for engineers and people-ops hires. Meant to be light, repeatable, and to reduce cognitive load for new hires while giving managers a clear 30-day impact backlog.

Scope: applies to all new hires (US/EMEA) joining engineering, product, and platform teams. Excludes contractors with short-term (<30d) engagements (see contractor-lite checklist).

Owner: Priya Nanduri (people-ops) — reach out in #people-ops-onboard for exceptions.

Before Day 0 (actions team):
- Create Welcome Slack channel and add hire + manager + mentor.
- Provision laptop order (hw ticket) and send logistics note.
- Populate first-week calendar slots (intro, manager 1:1s, mentor pairing).

Day 0 access model (deferred-access principle):
- Immediate: email, Slack, SSO core apps (Okta) scoped to role template, VPN, internal Wiki read-only.
- Delayed (granted after first-week checkpoint or security brief): write access to prod-adjacent repos, deploy pipelines, secret vault write permissions, internal billing dashboards.
- Justification step: manager must add short note in HR ticket when requesting elevated perms (what's the minimum scope + reason).

Reasoning: reduces blast-radius + decision fatigue. Quiet-start hires can start with sandboxed datasets and infra while ramping permissions as they demonstrate need.

Priority Skill Map (first 30 days) — template for manager to fill:
- Core product knowledge (must-have): README tour, system diagram, two short demos.
- Dev tooling fluency: repo checkout, CI run, local dev env within 2 days (goal).
- Observability basics: traces + logs for team services, how to run a local trace.
- Small impact task: identify a bug/cleanup or a doc improvement that ships in 30 days.
- Cross-team partner: intro to one adjacent team (infra/ops) and a paired 2-hour shadow.

Manager checklist (first 30 days):
- Day 0: 30-min manager kickoff (expectations + quiet-start contract).
- Days 1–3: mentor pairing, repo walkthrough, assign first small task.
- End of week 1: permissions review + escalate any missing access.
- End of week 4: 30-day impact review (1 pager + demo).

Mentor micro-rotation (recommended cadence):
- Weeks 1–2: daily 30m pairing focused on repo & infra.
- Weeks 3–4: twice-weekly 1h pairing on product context and the impact task.

Kickoff agenda (30min):
- Quick intros (5m), Team mission & 30d goals (7m), Immediate tasks + first PR (8m), Permissions plan + security brief (5m), Questions + next steps (5m).

Example 'first small task' ideas:
- fix flaky unit test and add an instability note to the test-runner docs
- add a short example to the public SDK README that reproduces a common error
- tidy up an internal runbook section (observability ↔ incident steps)

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- Do we need a different default template for SRE vs platform engineers? (SRE minimal access may differ).
- Can security approve a one-click ephemeral token flow for early sandboxing? (chasing SEC-ops, ticket SEC-77)

Linked tickets & refs:
- onboarding central checklist: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/HR/Onboarding+central
- quiet-start policy draft: HRON-412
- infra sandbox PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/internal-onboard/pull/58

Next steps / action items:
- People-ops to pilot with 3 hires in March (owners: Priya / Marco).
- Collect feedback via short pulse at day7 + day30 (Google form link to be added).
- Iterate permission templates and add role-specific variants for SRE / infra.

Notes to self: keep this intentionally lightweight. Managers often over-provision for speed — remind them that deferred access reduces cognitive load for new hires and risk for platform.

Status: draft -> share with security + infra for input; incorporate SRE template suggestions and then publish canonical wiki page.
